Subject: Post-demo: token runway, peak TPS & $/1M pricing targets

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today, Sara — really appreciate the time. Quick recap from our side and three asks so we can size a pilot and surface pricing scenarios: 

Summary from demo:
- Primary workload: conversational summarization + search re-rank for clinical QA (responses average ~450 tokens).
- Expected cadence: steady daily traffic with regular spikes around 10am/2pm ET tied to batch ingestion.

What we need to finalize pricing scenarios: 
1) Target monthly token volume (range ok) — helps pick committed slab vs. usage.
2) Peak TPS during burst windows (how many concurrent generation requests per sec).
3) Target $/1M tokens you’d like to see (range or target CPX).

We put together a short spreadsheet with three scenarios (attached) that maps token volumes + peak TPS to per-1M pricing at different commitment levels. If you can reply with approximate ranges for (1)-(3) above, I’ll run a recommended pillot offer and propose a fast-start contract (3 months pilot + optional reserved uplift).

Next steps proposed:
- You reply with ranges for tokens & peak TPS by EOD tomorrow.
- We send a 3-month pilot SOW and a pricing anchor by Friday.

Attachments: hosted-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (pricing scenarios), Lumos-demo-notes.pdf (demo highlights).

Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-demo: token runway, peak TPS & $/1M pricing targets

Thanks Rishi — great walkthrough. Below are the ballpark numbers from our side; still validating with engineering + procurement but these are the ranges we expect: 

1) Monthly token volume (range): 50,000,000 – 120,000,000 tokens/month. Our preferred starting commit for a pilot would be ~60,000,000 tokens/month.
2) Peak TPS: baseline ~10 TPS, but we see burst windows up to 40–60 TPS for 2–4 minute windows during ingestion runs. Sustained concurrency rarely exceeds 8–12 TPS outside bursts.
3) Target $/1M tokens: procurement is looking for guidance but target range is $12–$18 per 1M tokens for a committed pilot. If the SLA and SOC2 + KMS are in place, they might approve higher.

Other asks:
- Can you include a line for burst headroom (how we would be billed when bursts exceed committed TPS)?
- Have SOC2 Type II report and basic SSO/SCIM support documented — procurement will want those artifacts.

Happy to kick off a 3-month pilot at 60M tokens/month if the economics map reasonably to the $12–$18/1M range.

Sara Lin
Dir. Product Ops, Lumos Health

Subject: Re: Post-demo: token runway, peak TPS & $/1M pricing targets

Thanks, Sara — this is perfect context. Quick notes and how we’d model the pilot: 

A) Mapping your ranges to three pricing scenarios (see attached spreadsheet):
- Scenario A (pilot commit 60M/mo): anchor price $16/1M tokens, with billed burst fractional surcharge for tokens beyond committed slab. We model expected monthly spend ≈ $960/mo at nominal usage (60M * $16/1M).
- Scenario B (40–80M range): tiered pricing with $18/1M for <40M, $15/1M for 40–80M, $12/1M for >80M if you convert to reserved after pilot.
- Scenario C (higher: 100–120M): negotiated reserved rate $10–12/1M with guaranteed latency SLOs.

B) Peak TPS & burst handling:
- We support short bursts beyond committed TPS with an automated fallback to compatible model variant and a burst surcharge. For planning, assume we can absorb bursts up to +50% of the committed concurrency without queueing; anything >50% will be served at the fallback tier at ~x1.2 surcharge on per-token bill. We’ll reflect the burst surcharge in the spreadsheet.

C) Artifacts & compliance:
- I’ve attached SOC2 artifacts links in the shared Drive link. We also support SSO/SCIM provisioning; I’ll include a short checklist in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) Can your procurement confirm whether the pilot needs a PO or a signed SOW only?
2) If procurement is aligned, we’ll send a redlineable 3-month pilot SOW + pricing anchor tomorrow.
3) Internal: Camila — please prepare a conservative SLA-backed pricing anchor for 60M commit and include the burst surcharge line item. Marissa — please include a short note on expected latency SLO at 40–60 TPS bursts.

I’ll loop in our Solutions Engineer if we need deeper TPS validation.

Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
